_doc: qal/ptu -- THE MATCHED COMPARISON. Does the PULSED-INDUCTOR (current-ramp) top-up avoid the step-coupling damage the SWITCHED CLAMP (voltage-step) inflicts on the feeding stage, and does it change the settling, the pull-up overdrive, or the HIGH/LOW separation by depth?
pre_registration: PRE_REGISTERED.json, SOLE file on disk at 2026-09-29 01:30:52.417 -0700 (mtime is the proof); first new deck run at 01:31
own_cache: PYMS_VAE_CACHE=<scratchpad>/vae_cache_ptu, built from scratch; no .so copied from any sibling

HEADLINE.Q_does_the_pulsed_form_avoid_the_step_co: NO. REFUTED, and this is the run's main result. The coupling is proportional to HOW MUCH RAIL IS DELIVERED, not to the FORM of the delivery. Measured predecessor-LOW lift per mV of rail actually delivered: CLAMP 0.165 mean / 0.214 median (n=11); CORRECTED PULSED 0.447 mean / 0.355 median (n=4). Per volt delivered the pulsed form couples about TWICE AS HARD, not less. Its smaller absolute damage number (+5 to +42 mV against the clamp's +73 to +157 mV) is bought entirely by delivering 5x less rail.
HEADLINE.Q_is_the_committed_negative_result_an_ar: NO. The committed verdict does NOT need amending on its bottom line.
HEADLINE.Q_does_it_change_the_settling: NO, and it is WORSE than no top-up at all. At the headline point (s4, T=200 ps, dV=1.2) stage 3 reads 39.20% free, 49.65% clamped, and 33.08-34.08% under the corrected pulsed form.
HEADLINE.Q_does_it_move_the_pull_up: NO. Stage 3's rail is 0.765884 V free, 1.069085 V clamped, and 0.668973-0.737441 V under the corrected pulsed form -- BELOW the free control. The pMOS overdrive over the MEASURED |Vtp| = 0.4403 V therefore gets WORSE, not better, and the device constant still binds.
HEADLINE.Q_does_it_move_the_HIGH_LOW_separation: NO meaningful change, and the brief's premise about the separation is itself mis-attributed -- see SEPARATION below.
HEADLINE.A1_best_row: r_s4_rtu_T200_dv1000 -- the committed ideal-source bounding row, unchanged

WHAT_THE_CLAMP_IS_AND_IS_NOT_A_BOUND_ON.A7_claim_under_test: skiptu AMENDMENT A7: the clamp 'restores the rail as hard as a supply can, so it upper-bounds what ANY top-up can do for settling.'
WHAT_THE_CLAMP_IS_AND_IS_NOT_A_BOUND_ON.verdict: SOUND AS USED, with one clause that should be narrowed.
WHAT_THE_CLAMP_IS_AND_IS_NOT_A_BOUND_ON.sound_part: the clamp IS an upper bound on RAIL RESTORATION (+472 mV against the pulsed form's +88 mV at the matched point) and therefore on the settling that rail restoration can buy. The corrected pulsed form does not come close to it at any operating point measured.
WHAT_THE_CLAMP_IS_AND_IS_NOT_A_BOUND_ON.clause_to_narrow: 'upper-bounds what ANY top-up can do for settling' is too strong as a universal, because the clamp introduces its own damage term (backward coupling into the predecessor's LOW outputs) that costs stage 2 between 6.7 and 13.6 settling points. A form that delivered the same rail with less coupling would beat it on the chain minimum. The measurement here is that THE PULSED INDUCTOR IS NOT THAT FORM -- it couples harder per volt delivered. So A7's conclusion survives; only its generality over unbuilt forms is unsupported.

D1_THE_DELIVERY_SLOPE_on_the_topped_rail._units: V/ns, max RISING dV/dt on rail3, centred difference on the printed grid, over a window computed per row from its OWN schedule: [open[0]+EDGE, min(bound[3], close[1])-EDGE] so no hop switching is ever inside it
D1_THE_DELIVERY_SLOPE_on_the_topped_rail.READING: the pulsed form IS gentler -- by about 2.5x -- but the brief's stronger claim, that a di/dt-limited delivery has 'no voltage discontinuity to couple capacitively', is NOT what the waveform shows. 92 V/ns is a steep edge. The inductor limits the current, but the OUT switch still closes onto the rail and the stored inductor current still dumps into it, so the rail still steps.

D2_THE_DAMAGE_on_the_actual_victim._victim: stage 2's PULL-DOWN output nodes o2_1, o2_3, o2_5, o2_7 (SK.is_hi(2,i) true), measured in the same window as D1
D2_THE_DAMAGE_on_the_actual_victim._metric: worst LOW-node lift in mV, and the part ATTRIBUTABLE to the top-up = (topped row) - (free control at the same T, dV, same window)
D2_THE_DAMAGE_on_the_actual_victim.clamp_is_MONOTONE_in_its_own_strength: t_on 10 -> 20 -> 40 ps gives +72.8 -> +113.8 -> +157.4 mV, which is the mechanism confirming itself

THE_FAIR_COMPARISON_damage_per_mV_of_rai.READING: the pulsed form is about 2x WORSE per volt delivered. The step coupling is NOT an artefact of the clamp's form.

D5_THE_RAIL_DELIVERED.VERDICT: the corrected pulsed form cannot exceed the clamp's rail; it cannot even reach the FREE control's rail. The pull-up does not improve, it degrades. The device constant binds for a better reason than before: the preferred form was run at chain scale WITH the switch-node capacitance restored and the corrected gate sequence, and it still cannot raise the rail.

SEPARATION_D6.the_briefs_comparator_is_MIS_ATTRIBUTED: the series 528.68 / 22.89 / 1.52 / 0.122 / 0.010 / 0.001 mV belongs to qal/restore5's UNRESTORED ADJACENT cascade (row k6_T300_control), NOT to the skip chain. Reproduced here exactly from restore5/RESULTS.json: 528.6756 / -22.8913 / 1.5162 / -0.1221 / 0.0101 / -0.0009 mV. Note the SIGNS: from bank 2 on it is not merely small, it is INVERTED.

the_SKIP_chain_does_NOT_reproduce_that_c.READING: at dV = 1.2 every bank in every form is two to three orders of magnitude ABOVE the 3.42 mV sigma-Vt floor. The skip schedule re-powers banks 3 and 4 from fresh inductive hops off the ideally pre-charged head banks, so the level is regenerated rather than passed down a chain. The brief's 'separation still collapses below sigma-Vt by depth 3' is FALSE for this topology.

SEPARATION_D6.where_the_depth_effect_DOES_appear: the 5-bank chain, where bank 5's predecessor rail itself came from a hop: free s5 stage 5 separation is -24.075 mV at T=200 and -13.548 mV at T=300 -- INVERTED. And at dV = 1.5 the 4-bank chain degrades too (free stage 3 1.398 mV at T=300, below the floor; stage 4 inverted).
SEPARATION_D6.effect_of_top_up_form_on_separation: NONE that rescues it. Under the corrected pulsed form s4/T200/dV1.5 stage 4 is -40.796 mV (inverted), the same failure the free and clamped rows show at that dV.

INSTRUMENT_AND_HONESTY.A5_digit_check: PASS. VBEND 0.7138163 (rel 0.0), VBPK 0.8368896 (rel 0.0), t_hop 65.49500982 ps vs committed 65.49500982344826 (rel 1.85e-11), 8/8 cells at 100.000000%, 120/129 mt0 keys BIT-IDENTICAL against the committed mt0 (worst rel 6.24e-07 on QGT_Z, a t=0 pedestal). Decks are md5-identical byte copies of qal/lsweep/h_L15_W30_dv120.cir and p_L15_W30_dv120.cir.
independent_cross_checks_of_the_harness: my extractor reproduces EVERY committed free and rtu row's per-stage worst-gate percentage digit-for-digit from the .mt0 (e.g. free s4/T200/dV1.2 = 99.95/60.65/39.20/63.52; rtu = 99.95/50.56/49.65/95.66)
my hop-zero probes reproduce the committed A4 table exactly: hop 2 zero = 95.506 / 95.174 / 94.946 ps at T = 120 / 160 / 200 ps
restore5's unrestored separation series reproduced to 4 decimal places

A6_INSTRUMENT_GATE_FAILURE_reported_not_.statement: ALL 11 of my corrected pulsed rows FAIL the pre-registered 1.0 uA interrupted-inductor-current gate, at 112.4 to 132.5 uA. So do all 7 measurable committed ptu rows, at 110.7 to 122.4 uA. The free rows (0.0027-0.0162 uA) and the clamp rows (0.0017-0.0187 uA) PASS.
A6_INSTRUMENT_GATE_FAILURE_reported_not_.ROOT_CAUSE_located_in_the_committed_harn: AMENDMENT A8's fix -- 'in a PROBE deck the top-up DEVICES are still instantiated (so their loading is in the measurement) but are held permanently OFF' -- is implemented ONLY in tu.deck's RESISTIVE branch, as `L += SK.supply_tg(k, total_um, None, 'topup')`. The PULSED branch has no equivalent: it `continue`s, so the top-up devices are not instantiated in a ptu probe deck AT ALL. PROVEN on disk: the ptu-mode hop-1 probe deck p1_z_s4_ptu_T200_dv1200_L1_t12_C8_f.cir contains ZERO XTUSW/CNA lines while its row deck R_s4_ptu_T200_dv1200_L1_t12_C8.cir contains 4. skiptu/go.py compounds this with `zmode = 'rtu' if mode == 'rtu' else 'free'`, which routes ptu rows to free-mode zeros outright.
A6_INSTRUMENT_GATE_FAILURE_reported_not_.consequence: the pulsed top-up's hop zeros cannot be probed correctly by this harness as written. My A8 bootstrap (free zeros -> measured tfw -> re-probe in ptu mode) did not help, because the ptu probe deck is electrically identical to the free one -- and indeed it returned the same zero, 97.977 ps.
A6_INSTRUMENT_GATE_FAILURE_reported_not_.what_this_does_and_does_not_undermine: It means every CHAIN-level pulsed number in this run, and in the committed run, is instrumentally compromised at the ~9% level (122 uA against a ~1300 uA peak). It does NOT undermine the two load-bearing results, because: (1) the CLAMP rows, which carry the step-coupling measurement, PASS the gate; (2) the central claim that the pulsed form cannot deliver charge is established INDEPENDENTLY on a small fixture with no hops at all, hence no hop-zero to get wrong.

ROWS_NOT_MEASURED_stated_plainly.why: their top-up ZCS probe deck fails to CONVERGE, not to finish: q3_tz_s5_T300_dv1200_L1_t24_C8.cir stops at t = 198.0 ps of a 1600 ps transient -- at hop 1's switch close -- with 19 failed steps and 8 nonlinear failures, after which every .measure reports FAILED. Re-run twice with the same result, so it is reproducible and not contention.
ROWS_NOT_MEASURED_stated_plainly.coverage_gap_that_remains: the 5-bank (s5) topology under the CORRECTED pulsed top-up is NOT measured. dV coverage is complete (1.0 / 1.2 / 1.5) and T coverage is complete (120/160/200/300) in the 4-bank topology via the t_on = 24 ps rows.

A_SCHEDULING_RESULT_that_is_not_bookkeep.statement: the fixture-mandated gate sequence costs SLEW + 4*EDGE = 32 ps of preparation before the pulse can start (the high side must be fully on while the low side still clamps na, or na is yanked negative -- A6). At T = 120 ps the whole hold window between hop 1's measured zero (297.98 ps) and bank 3's stage boundary (320.00 ps) is 22.0 ps. The preparation ALONE exceeds it.
A_SCHEDULING_RESULT_that_is_not_bookkeep.measured_consequence: at T = 120 the pulse ENDS 33.98 ps (t_on=12) or 45.98 ps (t_on=24) AFTER the boundary at which the settling is read; at T = 160 with t_on = 24 it ends 5.98 ps after. Those rows are reported, but their top-up has not delivered anything by the instant the measurement is taken -- confirmed by the waveform: rail3 rise over the window is 0.0 mV at T = 120 and T = 160.
A_SCHEDULING_RESULT_that_is_not_bookkeep.why_it_matters: T = 120 and 160 ps are exactly where the free chain CLEARS the 0.4400 V threshold. So a correctly-sequenced pulsed top-up is unavailable precisely where the schedule otherwise works.

THE_SMALL_FIXTURE_the_clean_evidence._why_it_is_the_clean_evidence: one linear capacitor, no hops, no schedule -- so no hop zero to get wrong and none of the A6/A8 contamination above. The standing directive is to prove a mechanism on a small fixture and use full scale as confirmation only.
THE_SMALL_FIXTURE_the_clean_evidence.fixture: 28.98 fF bank pre-charged to the chain's OWN measured free rail3 of 0.765884 V, supply 1.2 V, wsw = 10 um, tucell.py's corrected gate sequence, freewheel cut at its MEASURED current zero
THE_SMALL_FIXTURE_the_clean_evidence.grid: Cna {8, 20, 50} fF x Ltu {1, 5, 15} nH x t_on {6, 12, 24} ps = 27 points
THE_SMALL_FIXTURE_the_clean_evidence.A7_EXTRAPOLATION_REFUTED: skiptu A7 swept the switch-node capacitance only to the DERIVED 8 fF, and its own table trends toward zero FROM BELOW (-15.735 fC at 2 fF, -2.560 at 8 fF), which invites the reading that a larger Cna would cross into positive delivery. MEASURED here: it does NOT. Cna = 20 fF and 50 fF are WORSE than 8 fF at every (Ltu, t_on). The trend is NOT monotone; it turns around. This is why the chain Cna sweep was cut to the DERIVED 8 fF -- small fixture first, full scale as confirmation only.
THE_SMALL_FIXTURE_the_clean_evidence.chain_scale_confirmation: at chain scale the corrected cell delivers q = -1.4 fC (t_on=12) to +9.3 fC (t_on=24) into two banks at s4/T200/dV1.2, Qmult -0.011 to +0.058, against a switch gate drive of 297.8 to 322.2 fJ. The gate drive alone is ~36x the committed single-hop dissipation of 8.3828 fJ.

WHAT_THE_A6_FIX_DID_ACHIEVE.statement: adding the A6-mandated switch-node capacitance and tucell's corrected sequence DOES largely repair the unholdable switch node at chain scale, which is a real improvement over the committed decks.
WHAT_THE_A6_FIX_DID_ACHIEVE.measured: V(na3) over [300,400] ps now has a minimum of -0.08179 V and reaches 1.09652 V (t_on=12) / 1.17222 V (t_on=24) against a 1.2 V supply. The A6 pathology was na driven to -0.30 to -0.42 V with the inductor reversed.
WHAT_THE_A6_FIX_DID_ACHIEVE.and_yet: delivery is still ~zero and the rail still ends BELOW the free control. So the switch node was a real defect, it has been largely fixed, and fixing it does not rescue the mechanism.

INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks._probe_vs_row: q3_*/q4_* hold VGTO_k high to 4400p, past the 1100p transient end -- they are the A1 probe-then-cut INSTRUMENT, not results. Only the 11 r_s4_ptu_* are row decks.
INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks.operating_points_covered: ONE: s4, T = 200 ps, dV = 1.2, L_hop = 15 nH / W = 30 um. The filename sweep is over the top-up knobs only (Ltu {1,2,5,15} nH x t_on {6,12,24} ps). No dV = 1.0 or 1.5, no T = 120/160/300, no 5-bank.
INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks.mt0_present: 7 of 11 row decks; 5 of those carry complete stage-3 and stage-4 settling (the other 2 had rail3 driven below the 0.02 V guard, which is itself the pathology)
INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks.IS_per_gate_settling_present: YES -- the brief's premise that they 'carry charge measures but apparently NOT per-gate settling' is WRONG on disk. Every ptu deck writes O1_0S..O4_7E, G2_*/G3_*/G4_*, VR{1..4}K{1..4}, VR{1..4}PK/MN. Everything the committed settling convention needs is present.
WHY_THEY_WENT_UNREPORTED_four_independen: 1. They FAIL the pre-registered A6 gate at 110.7-122.4 uA against 1.0 uA, for the tu.deck root cause documented above.

2. They carry NO switch-node capacitance -- AMENDMENT A6 rules that any buck number taken without it 'is an artefact of the shim'. mtimes prove the ordering: the chain ptu decks were written 21:56-21:59, the small fixture that DISCOVERED the defect at 22:05-22:09, and tu.py NEVER emits a CNA even in its final 22:17 version.
3. They use the pre-A6 gate sequence (simultaneous make-before-break), not tucell's corrected early-HS / slewed-LS / OUT-last sequence.

4. Their per-stage settling reproduces, digit for digit, the seven values AMENDMENT A5 names as DISCARDED and not to be quoted: L1/t6 41.14, L1/t12 36.96, L1/t24 33.87, L2/t12 40.10, L2/t24 34.25, L5/t6 71.75, L5/t12 71.13.
INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks.what_they_already_showed: every one delivered NEGATIVE charge into both topped banks (-5.2 to -45.7 fC), and drove the topped rails negative (VR3K3 = -0.1407 V, VR4K4 = -0.1141 V in the L5/t12 row). A7's fixture pathology, reproduced at chain scale.
INVENTORY_of_the_34_committed_ptu_decks.SO_THE_SUBSTITUTION_WAS_NOT_SILENT: AMENDMENT A7 states the substitution explicitly, gives the measurement behind it, and labels every rtu row an ideal-source booking. The gap this run closes is not a concealment; it is that the pulsed form was abandoned BEFORE the two fixes the small fixture forced were ever carried back into the chain.

RE_VERDICT_against_the_SAME_pre_register.A1_every_gate_in_every_stage_90pct: FAIL, in every form, at every operating point. Best corrected-pulsed row 34.08%; best row anywhere still the committed ideal-source clamp row at 59.48%.
RE_VERDICT_against_the_SAME_pre_register.A2_delivered_input_HIGH_0p4400_at_every_: one corrected-pulsed row clears it -- s4 T=120 dV=1.2 t_on=24, min 0.4535 V -- but that row's top-up pulse ENDS 45.98 ps AFTER the stage boundary, so it is the FREE chain's result, not the top-up's. The committed positive result stands unchanged: the skip schedule clears 0.4400 V at short beats WITHOUT any top-up (best minimum 0.531571 V).
RE_VERDICT_against_the_SAME_pre_register.DOES_THE_COMMITTED_VERDICT_NEED_AMENDING: NO on its bottom line, and it now rests on a stronger footing than before: the architecture's preferred pulsed-inductor form has been run at CHAIN scale with the switch-node capacitance restored and the corrected gate sequence installed, and it still cannot raise the rail, still cannot reach 90%, and couples backward into the feeding stage HARDER per volt delivered than the clamp does.
WHAT_SHOULD_BE_AMENDED: A7's clause 'it upper-bounds what ANY top-up can do for settling' should be narrowed to 'upper-bounds what any top-up can do BY RAIL RESTORATION'. The clamp carries a damage term of its own (stage 2: 60.65% -> 47.02-54.00%) and is therefore not a uniform upper bound on the chain minimum over all conceivable forms. It remains a valid bound against every form actually built.

A8 should be recorded as UNFIXED ON THE ptu PATH. The 'instantiate the idle devices in the probe deck' fix exists only in tu.deck's resistive branch; the pulsed branch continues past it. Until that is repaired, no pulsed row from this harness -- committed or new -- can pass the A6 gate.
The record should note that the pulsed top-up's corrected gate sequence needs 32 ps of preparation, which does not fit inside the hold window at T <= 160 ps.

ARTEFACTS.PRE_REGISTERED.json: acceptance + falsifiable expectations, sole file on disk at 01:30:52
ARTEFACTS.EXISTING.json: per-gate settling, rails, LOW/HIGH and top-up meters extracted from all 34 committed ptu decks plus the free/rtu rows
ARTEFACTS.FIXTURE.json: the 27-point Cna x Ltu x t_on sweep of the corrected top-up cell
ARTEFACTS.COUPLING.json / COUPLING2.json: D1 delivery slope and D2 predecessor-LOW lift, per row, on per-row windows
ARTEFACTS.SLOPES.json: the first-pass slope scan on the committed decks
ARTEFACTS.SEPARATION.json: D6 by bank depth, with restore5's series recomputed
ARTEFACTS.COMPARE.json: the matched table and the re-verdict
ARTEFACTS.zeros.json / tu_zeros.json: every MEASURED hop zero and top-up freewheel zero, with the raw probe value and the 32 ps preparation offset recorded separately

LABELS.MEASURED: every settling, rail, LOW-node, slope, charge, separation and zero figure above
LABELS.DERIVED: the switch-node capacitance central estimate of ~8 fF (A6's own arithmetic); the damage-per-volt ratios
LABELS.ASSUMED: Cna itself, which is why it was swept over {8, 20, 50} fF on the fixture
LABELS.LOWER_BOUND: all device charge and energy numbers -- sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps. Per A6 this is FIRST-ORDER at a buck switch node, which is why CNA is explicit here.
LABELS.SCOPE: all numbers are SHALLOW-STACK (sg13g2_o21ai_1 never settles anywhere in the PDK envelope)
